note: Experimental operator-card surface. V128 policy: coarse obligation classes route machinery; fine cards and GP-219 handles are recall, receipt, and nearest-confuser surfaces. V177R narrows the active carrier to action-constraint content; field names are scaffold and routing support.

obligation_route.evidence_basis: v128b/v128d: binary covered-vs-none and coarse obligations are more reliable than full/partial labels.
obligation_route.falsifier: the boundary is asserted without a checkable pass/fail condition
obligation_route.name: Bound / Boundary
owes: the claimed bound, boundary, or update
the pass/fail condition that blocks overclaim

obligation_route.evidence_basis: v128d: construct is one of the four higher-reliability obligation classes.
obligation_route.falsifier: the object exists only as prose, or the claimed property is not checked on the object
obligation_route.name: Construct / Witness
owes: the property it is meant to witness
the check that would falsify the witness

top_cards.boundary: This supports only the named claim update, not the broader thesis.
top_cards.breaker: Find a case where the carrier is true but the claim update is false, or where the carrier is confounded.
entry_conditions: A claim depends on an indirect signal, proxy, benchmark, theorem import, or measurement.
The next update is unsafe unless the evidence carrier is named and tested.
top_cards.name: Evidence-Carrier Routing
required_output: 4-row table: claim, carrier, receipt needed, failure condition.
One boundary sentence saying what cannot yet be claimed.
steps: Name the evidence carrier that would license that update.
State the receipt that makes the carrier admissible.
State what observation invalidates the carrier.
top_cards.stop_update_rule: Do not update the claim until the carrier receipt is present and the breaker has been checked.
